access_key_read_only_label: Read-only — never mints a Key, changes a password or mints an Invite
access_key_secret_once: Copy this now — it is shown once and never again.
account_invite_blurb: This one-use Invite creates your account and Home Kitchen.
account_recover_blurb: This one-use recovery link is spent when you set your new password.
account_setup_blurb: The first person here becomes this kitchen's Operator.
arrived_created_line: {title} arrived, with every version the file carried.
arrived_extended_line: {title} was already here, and the file carried it further. What it held past what you had is on it now.
arrived_kept: Kept as a recipe of your own
arrived_passengers: {recipes} travelled inside it, because this recipe is made of them.
arrived_passengers_one: {recipes} travelled inside it, because this recipe is made of it.
arrived_unchanged_line: {title} is already here, exactly as the file has it. Nothing was written.
bring_in_file_full: Add a recipe from a recipe file
bring_in_link_full: Add a recipe from a link
bring_in_unreadable: That file is not a recipe file Kamosu could read.
component_pick_closest: Nothing matched closely. These are the nearest.
component_pick_failed: Your recipes could not be searched just now.
component_pick_nothing: No recipe matched. Kamosu never guesses which recipe a line means, so nothing is offered here until you find it.
cook_failed: Could not start cooking this recipe.
cook_false_start_confirm: Throw this cooking away? Starting counts as a cooking, so this is how a false start is undone.
cook_finished: Cooked. Add a rating or a note in the diary whenever you like.
cook_insert_step: Insert a step before this one
cook_no_steps: This recipe has no steps to cook through.
cook_nothing_new: Nothing new to add — just the pot.
cook_photo_failed: That photograph couldn't be kept on this phone.
cook_photo_take: Take a photograph of this cooking
cook_write_failed: Could not save what you did. It is still on screen.
cooked_blurb: Every cooking you started, newest first — finished or not.
cooked_delete_confirm: Delete it? A cooking deleted is gone for good.
cooked_empty: Nothing cooked yet. Start cooking a recipe and it lands here, whether or not you ever finish it.
cooked_failed: The diary could not be read. Kamosu may be restarting.
cooked_gone: This recipe is no longer on your shelf.
divergence_leaving: leaving your recipe when you save
divergence_nothing_to_carry: Nothing to carry — this one is yours already.
divergence_put_away: Just the recipe. {count} differences put away.
divergence_said_added: {kitchen} wrote this after you parted. You haven’t got it.
divergence_said_removed: {kitchen} took this out. You still have it in yours.
divergence_said_yours_only: You wrote this after you parted. {kitchen} hasn’t got it.
divergence_save_hint: Written for you as a sentence, and yours to rewrite. Kamosu stores what you say happened, not a pointer at {kitchen}’s recipe.
divergence_saved: Saved. Those lines are part of your recipe now.
divergence_take_remove: Take it out of mine as well
divergence_too_many: This recipe has {count} Branches on this Kamosu. The switch reads two, so yours is shown on its own.
divergence_unsaved: {count} lines from {kitchen}, sitting on your recipe. Not saved.
divergence_unsaved_one: One line from {kitchen}, sitting on your recipe. Not saved.
divergence_unshared_one: One line you and {kitchen} don’t share
home_blurb: Four ways in, worked out from what you have.
home_empty: Nothing is cooking yet. What you start will wait for you here.
home_empty_why: Home is worked out from your own recipes and your own cooking, so it fills itself in as you go. Right now there is nothing to work from.
home_failed: Kamosu could not work out your shelves just now.
home_shelf_cooked_most_why: What you keep coming back to
import_crouton_blurb: Move your Crouton library here: choose the zip Crouton exports, or a single .crumb. Importing the same library again later updates what is here instead of doubling it.
import_crouton_last: See the last Crouton import's report
kitchen_invite_secret_once: Copy this now — it is shown once and never again.
meaning_now_on: Meaning search is on. Try that search again.
meaning_what_it_costs: It needs {model}, which Kamosu does not ship. Turning it on downloads the model — about 220 MB — and means accepting Google's terms for it.
measures_explained: How much a line means for you, on one line beneath it. Kamosu never rewrites the recipe, always says about, and says nothing where the line is already in your measures. American is the default, as a stated convention: a cup is 240 ml, a tablespoon 15 ml, a teaspoon 5 ml.
offline_cached: This recipe isn't in your Kitchen. You're reading the copy kept when you opened it on {date}.
offline_held: Every recipe in your Kitchen is on this phone. Cooking and your list work as usual; changing a recipe waits for the server.
offline_insecure_body: Kamosu is reached over http://, so it can't keep anything on this phone for when there's no signal. Whoever runs this Kamosu can give it an https:// address.
offline_install_apple: Safari deletes what Kamosu keeps for offline after 7 days without a visit. From the Home Screen it keeps it, and opens like an app.
offline_install_other: Installed, Kamosu opens like an app and keeps its offline copy.
offline_install_other_step: Open your browser's menu and choose Install, or Add to Home screen
offline_library_body: {count} recipes and their pictures, about {size}. Best fetched on wifi.
offline_library_title: Your library isn't on this phone yet
offline_phone_installed: On your Home Screen, so what Kamosu keeps here stays.
offline_phone_kept: {count} recipes kept on this phone, brought up to date {date}.
offline_phone_secure: Reached securely, so Kamosu can keep your recipes here for when there's no signal.
offline_unfilled: Your library isn't on this phone yet, so only what you've opened is here. Changing a recipe waits for the server.
offline_waits_bring_in: Bringing a recipe in waits for the server
offline_waits_bring_in_row: Bringing a recipe in waits for the server
offline_waits_copy: Taking a Copy waits for the server
offline_waits_file: The recipe file waits for the server
offline_waits_import_link: Importing from a link waits for the server
offline_waits_keep: Keeping it waits for the server
reading_failed: That Reading could not be saved.
reading_names_recipe: This line names a recipe: {title}. Correct the amount to change how much of it is wanted.
reading_no_version: The line above is untouched. Correcting a Reading is not an edit to the recipe and makes no Version.
reading_not_recipe: This line is not a recipe
reading_will_name: This line will name {title}. Save the Reading to keep it.
recipe_as_cooked_lines: The lines as you cooked them
recipe_component_method_below: Its method is at the foot of the page ↓
recipe_cooked_differently_on: On {when}, you cooked this recipe with words of your own.
recipe_failed: This recipe could not be read.
recipe_keep_as_version: Keep it as a new Version
recipe_moved_on_since: The recipe has changed since you cooked it. Keeping this replaces what it says now — Kamosu never combines two versions of a dish.
recipe_print_failed: The sheet could not be made. Try again in a moment.
recipe_promote_failed: Could not keep it. Nothing about the recipe changed.
recipe_promoted: Kept. It is a Version on this recipe now, and the cooking still says which one it cooked.
recipes_blurb: One shelf, and a result that says what matched.
recipes_empty: The shelf is empty. The first recipe you write or import lands here.
recipes_failed: The shelf could not be read. Kamosu may be restarting.
recipes_import_unreadable: That page holds no recipe Kamosu could read.
recipes_nothing_meaning: Meaning search finds a recipe when you describe it rather than name it.
recipes_nothing_why: Kamosu looked through every title, ingredient and step on your shelf, and your own cooking notes. Meaning search is off on this Kamosu, so it matched the words themselves.
recipes_nothing_why_meaning: Kamosu looked through every title, ingredient and step on your shelf, your own cooking notes, and what each recipe means — and nothing came close enough.
report_bare: {count} came as just a name and a link: {titles}.
report_changed: {title} changed in Crouton since the last import. Yours was kept as it is: the change is held, not written over.
report_extra_photo_many: Left out: {count} extra photos from {title}. A recipe keeps one photo, so add them to steps by hand if you want them.
report_extra_photo_one: Left out: one extra photo from {title}. A recipe keeps one photo, so add it to a step by hand if you want it.
report_needs_you_waiting: Once everything is in, Kamosu looks for recipes that share a name or a web page and asks whether to link them.
report_pairs_blurb: These share a name or a page. Tick the ones that are two takes on the same dish: they'll show each other as Related Recipes. Nothing is merged.
report_running: {done} of {total} recipes in so far. You can leave this page: the import keeps going, and this report stays here.
report_site_icons: Left out: {count} website icons. They're the site's logo, not a photo of the dish.
report_title_file: The recipe file you brought in
report_unreadable_photos: {title} arrived without its photo: the picture couldn't be read.
settings_agent_reads: An agent does what it is told, including by text it reads. An agent holding your Access Key reads recipe pages other people wrote, and Kamosu cannot tell an instruction from an ingredient. A read-only Key limits what that costs; nothing prevents it.
settings_hand_unverified: A Hand is a reminder of who wrote a Version, never proof. Anyone editing a recipe file can put any name in it.
settings_meaning_catching_up: {count} recipes have changed since the index was last read. Kamosu catches up within the minute.
settings_meaning_declined: Off. You declined the model's terms, so Kamosu searches by words alone.
settings_meaning_off: Off. The model's terms are accepted, so turning it on needs no new agreement.
settings_meaning_on: On, using {model}. Searching matches on meaning as well as on words.
settings_operator_boundary: The Operator boundary is a courtesy, not a wall: whoever holds the disk holds everything.
settings_share_no_unsay: Ending a Share Link stops new arrivals. It reaches no copy already sent.
settings_stolen_phone: A stolen unlocked phone is a logged-in phone. Sessions never expire, because a timer would fire on a phone that spent a fortnight offline at the stove rather than on a thief. End the session from another device instead.
settings_stranger_waits: Someone holding a Share Link can make another stranger wait. Work nobody signed in for runs one piece at a time, so a crowd becomes a queue rather than a fallen-over server. Your own cooking is never behind it.
settings_unaudited: Nobody has audited Kamosu. It is a recipe app written for one household and shared.
share_address_hint: Where people reach this Kamosu from outside, e.g. https://kamosu.example.com. Asked once, and kept — a link is stored as a token, so changing the address later does not break a link already sent.
share_address_missing: A link needs an address people can open.
share_blurb: One permanent address, for anyone you send it to.
share_carries_components: This recipe includes {recipes}, which will be readable through this link. Nothing else changes: what a recipe includes gets no page and no link of its own, and is read only through this one.
share_failed: The link could not be changed.
share_file_carries: {recipes} travel inside it, because this recipe is made of them.
share_file_carries_one: {recipes} travels inside it, because this recipe is made of it.
share_file_holds: It holds {notes} and {photographs}, with every version back to the first.
share_file_missing: {count} photographs are no longer on this instance and will not be in the file.
share_file_missing_one: One photograph is no longer on this instance and will not be in the file.
share_file_opens: It opens anywhere, and another Kamosu takes it in whole.
share_file_waiting: What it holds waits for the server.
share_is_shared: Anyone with this link can read this recipe.
share_link_shown_once: Copy it now — Kamosu keeps only a fingerprint of this link and cannot show it to you again. Ending the link and turning it back on mints a new one.
share_not_shared: This recipe has no link. Only your Kitchen can see it.
share_standing: A share carries everything this recipe has ever been, back to its first version — every name and every note about what changed. Ending the link stops anyone new from opening it. It cannot reach a copy already sent.
shopping_blurb: A choice of recipes, not a list of things.
shopping_empty: No list yet. Choose the recipes you mean to cook and Kamosu writes one.
shopping_failed: Kamosu could not read your list just now. Try again in a moment.
shopping_send_failed: Kamosu could not copy the list. Select it and copy it by hand.
shopping_sent: Copied. Paste it wherever you keep your shopping.
shopping_typed_by_you: You typed this. Kamosu keeps it exactly as typed and merges it with nothing.
thread_blurb: Every save is a Version, in order. Nothing here is ever rewritten.
thread_cooking_failed: Could not start cooking this Version.
thread_cooking_started: Started — this Attempt is pinned to this Version.
thread_failed: The Thread could not be read.
thread_fork_detail: Kamosu worked this out by walking each Branch's chain back until they met — this is the last Version they share.
tokens_blurb: Every value below is read from the stylesheet this page loaded. Nothing here is maintained by hand.
tokens_specimen: The quick brown fox · Le renard brun saute par-dessus le chien paresseux
write_add_where: Return at the end of a line makes the next one. Both buttons drop the new thing in where the cursor is, and at the foot of the list when it is nowhere.
write_changed_now: Asked now, because it is true now and cannot be added later.
write_components_failed: The recipe was saved, but a line naming another recipe could not be marked. Open the line and try again.
write_move: Drag to move this line, or use the arrow keys
write_needs_both_yield: A Yield needs both a number and a word for what it makes.
write_needs_minutes: {field} must be whole minutes, or left empty.
write_needs_nutrition: The Nutrition figure has to be a number, or left empty.
write_nutrition_hint: Optional, and most recipes have none. Kamosu never works this figure out from the lines above.
write_outcome_unknown: Kamosu could not tell whose Kitchen this is, so it will not say what saving would do.
write_paste_fresh: Nothing is saved until you save.
write_paste_hint: Title, ingredients and method together. Kamosu says what it made of it before anything lands.
write_paste_no_title: No title in it, so type one in afterwards.
write_paste_nothing: There is nothing in that paste.
write_paste_replaces: This replaces the {ingredients} ingredients and {steps} steps already here. Nothing is saved until you save.
write_paste_start_here: Start the method at this line
write_photo_cover: or leave it, and a Cover gets drawn for you
write_photo_failed: That picture could not be kept.
write_said_fork: This recipe is not in one of your Kitchens. Saving does not change it. It starts your own {title} in {kitchen}, from this point, and the original stays where it is.
write_said_save: Saving writes a new Version onto your {title}, in {kitchen}.
write_saved_collapsed: This joined your last save rather than making a second entry in the Thread.
write_saved_copied: Your own copy is made. You are standing in it now.
write_step_rule: A Step is a sentence and, if you want one, a photograph. There is no timer, temperature or duration to fill in.
write_will_fork: This will start your own copy
